seoTitle: robots.txt Diff Tool: Compare Two Versions by Rule
metaDescription: Compare two robots.txt files and see added and removed rules per user-agent, ignoring comments, order and blank lines. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Compares an old and a new robots.txt by meaning, not by text, and lists the rules added or removed for each user-agent and each Sitemap line.
why:
A normal text diff buries the real change under moved lines, new comments and different spacing. What you need to know after a deploy is which crawler can now fetch or no longer fetch which paths.

This tool merges groups the way crawlers do, then compares the rules for each user-agent. If only comments or order changed, it says there are no rule changes. Paste archived copies to see how a policy changed over time; the site itself makes no network requests.
howTo: Paste the old robots.txt in the first box.
Paste the new one in the second box.
Read the changes grouped by user-agent.
Run the new file through the tester for your key URLs.

faq.q: Does the order of rules matter?
faq.a: Not for Google or RFC 9309 crawlers: the longest matching rule wins. The diff ignores order for that reason.

faq.q: Are two groups for the same bot merged?
faq.a: Yes. Crawlers combine them, so the diff does too before comparing.
